title: pseudoTarget inspector
blurb: Inspects event.pseudoTarget from live pointer/touch hits on ::before, ::after, and ::marker content, walks CSSPseudoElement.parent chains, and inspects nested ::view-transition-* chains.
question: Can event.pseudoTarget and CSSPseudoElement.parent chains expose the exact selector needed to re-select both simple generated content and nested view-transition pseudo-elements?
result: In Chrome 153 headless, real mouse clicks and touch taps on ::before, ::after, and ::marker return event.pseudoTarget with accurate .type values and walking a 4-level view-transition chain works via .pseudo() and .parent; selectorText is absent in Chrome 153 so nested snapshot disambiguation awaits Chrome 160+.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless) with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features on 2026-11-28; earlier Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12

friction.summary: Generated pseudo-elements (::before, ::after, ::marker) cannot receive keyboard focus to fire event.pseudoTarget
friction.repro: Tab through the ticket cards and list items; focus skips ::before, ::after, and ::marker boxes so keyboard-only users cannot trigger click hits with event.pseudoTarget directly.
friction.workaround: Provide native <button> controls that inspect the corresponding pseudo-elements via element.pseudo() as a keyboard-accessible equivalent.
